Subject: OrionPay post-incident summary & remediation plan (v1)

Ravi / OrionPay team, Kimberly, Sean, Laura, Rishi —

Attached: orionpay_postincident_summary_v1.pdf, perf-traces-20260624-06-25.zip, sla-credit-workbook.xlsx

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Impact window: 2026-06-24 23:38 UTC — 2026-06-25 02:05 UTC. Estimated affected sessions: ~3.8% of checkouts (sampled).
- Root cause: an interaction of an autoscaling edge-case with the runtime's continuous batching heuristics. Under a burst of heterogeneous short and long sequences the batching scheduler created high head-of-line latency; concurrent KV cache misses amplified per-token work for a subset of requests, producing elevated p95/p99 and occasional 5xx from resource exhaustion paths.
- Immediate mitigations applied: 1) temporarily tightened batching window for affected pool; 2) increased pre-warm workers in us-west for the workload; 3) pinned a safer model variant for high-throughput routes. Incident was contained at 02:05 UTC.

Planned corrective actions (owner / ETA):
- Adjust batching scheduler to avoid HLBT (head-of-line blocking) with mixed sequence distributions (Marcus Lin) — ETA: 2026-07-15 (can be canaried to staging 7/8).
- Improve KV cache warmup and add early-detection metrics for cache miss amplification (Rishi Malhotra) — ETA: 2026-07-09.
- Add per-customer circuit-breaker thresholds and auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant under high p99 (Kimberly Park + Engineering) — ETA: 2026-07-20.
- SLA credit calc: workbook attached; proposed credit equivalent to 6% of monthly commit for June window (Sean to confirm commercial terms).

Ask from OrionPay: review attached RCA and confirm acceptance or open follow-up questions. We propose an exec readout on Wed 2026-07-01 14:00 PT.

Notes: logs/traces attached. We will open OPS-4128 and link additional artifacts.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
